name: got
why: A version control system from the OpenBSD circle with a different design philosophy, an unusual take on a crowded category.

brief.what_it_is: Game of Trees (Got) is a version control system that its homepage says prioritizes ease of use and simplicity over flexibility. It stores its versioned data in Git repositories, so a repository can be worked on with both Got and Git. Git remains available for anything Got has not yet implemented. The homepage lists a 0.130 release, dated October 14, 2026, and a -portable 0.130 release dated October 16, 2026. The homepage does not describe inputs and outputs beyond this.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames Got as being developed on OpenBSD by OpenBSD developers and other contributors, mainly for OpenBSD developers' own version control needs, and later used more widely by Unix-like users. The page's quoted line jokes that no OpenBSD discussion is complete without a long thread about source control migration.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage says Got uses Git repositories as its storage format, so Git and Got can operate on the same repository. Git covers any functionality Got does not yet provide. The homepage does not explain the internals further.
brief.install_notes: The homepage has separate install paths by platform. OpenBSD has an Installation page. FreeBSD, NetBSD, Linux, DragonflyBSD and macOS each link to a 'Portable version' page. The scout notes list executables including got, gotd, gotwebd, gotctl, gotadmin, gotsh, gotwebctl, gitwrapper and tog. The homepage does not mention accounts, runtimes or configuration. The brew install itself was not checked.
brief.standout: Instead of competing on feature breadth, Got deliberately trades flexibility for simplicity and keeps Git repositories as its on-disk format, so it can be adopted without migrating data. It also ships a hosting daemon (gotd) and a web frontend (gotwebd) alongside the client.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the homepage shows: a 0.130 release dated October 14, 2026 (-portable 0.130 on October 16, 2026), with mailing lists, commit notifications and an IRC channel listed. I did not check the repository's commit history, so the most recent release date is the only evidence.
brief.caveats: The homepage says the main audience is OpenBSD developers, and the portable builds are secondary. Got is not a full Git replacement, and Git is still needed for functionality Got lacks. The homepage makes no explicit licence statement beyond saying it is under a BSD-style licence. The homepage gave no detail on feature gaps, and I did not open the Comparison or FAQ pages.
quotes: Game of Trees (Got) is a version control system which prioritizes ease of use and simplicity over flexibility.
Got uses Git repositories to store versioned data.
It will always remain possible to work with both Got and Git on the same repository.
No mention of openbsd on the internet is complete without a long thread about source control migration. — tedu@
fetch_log: https://gameoftrees.org/ — fetched OK; navigation lists the Manual Pages, Examples, FAQ, Comparison to CVS, SVN, and Git, and the Project Goals pages, but the page text gave no URLs for them, so I did not guess any. Stopped after one fetch because the homepage carried enough for the brief.
